messages.author: e32484f448e128cc
messages.subject: Suppress INLA-SPDE notes?
parts:
We've written a function that uses INLA-SPDE in the background to do part of our analysis. When calling INLA (in fact only the first time a user does that in a given session), a NOTE is printed saying:

Note: method with signature ‘TsparseMatrix#Matrix#missing#replValue’ chosen for function ‘[<-’,
 target signature ‘dgTMatrix#ngCMatrix#missing#numeric’.
 "Matrix#nsparseMatrix#missing#replValue" would also be valid

I understand this is not a problem --- in fact it doesn't happen when you re-run our function in the same session. But, as our function is intended for users who are probably not familiar with the whole INLA-SPDE machinery, we'd like to avoid printing this message. Is this possible at all?

Thanks
Gianluca

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Suppress INLA-SPDE notes?
parts:
I found the code I was thinking of,
options(list("Matrix.quiet"=TRUE))
but that doesn't actually turn off these messages. Looking in the
change log for the Matrix package indicates that that instead relates
to other types of messages, such as in the qr decomposition method,
see
?"sparseQR-class"

The problem with the "Note:" messages is that they are generated by
the S4 object system in the R language, and therefore hard to pin down
individually.
Since they are not warnings, don't use suppressWarnings(), as that
would disable _actual_ warnings!
A safer option is to use suppressMessages():

In new R session:
library(INLA)
Q=inla.spde.precision(inla.spde2.matern(inla.mesh.create(globe=4)),theta=c(0,0))
This should produce the Note:s.

In another new R session:
library(INLA)
suppressMessages({Q=inla.spde.precision(inla.spde2.matern(inla.mesh.create(globe=4)),theta=c(0,0))})
This should _not_ produce the Note:s. Other types of potentially
informative notes will also be disabled however,
so it's not a perfect solution.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Suppress INLA-SPDE notes?
parts:
Unfortunately these messages can happen in any place that does any sparse matrix operation, and the precise trigger depends on user input, so covering all possibilities in that way would be difficult; I've had messages appearing far into a long and complex R session.
We'd have to add a "dummy calculation" for every encountered case, and it's not necessarily clear how to construct a case that would trigger a specific Note.  That said, it shouldn't hurt to add dummy calculations that we _do_ know would trigger a Note.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Suppress INLA-SPDE notes?
parts: .

>
> Håvard's suggestion is of course very interesting, but, I think, in order to make sure the same note wouldn't show up, it means I should implement a set of fake objects to run the same analysis I need for my own code --- except I would suppressMessages this. I haven't tried very hard today (and will check again in the next couple of days), but I guess this may slow down the calculation (as effectively I would run a dummy analysis for nothing)...

Not quite; the initiation "dummy" operations don't even necessarily need to call _any_ functions from inla, but could use very small operands, and would only be needed once per R session. I think all the messages are due to "matrix of type A, binary operator, matrix of type B",
where the matrix types are automatically converted into compatible types for the operator. The issue is that there may be more than one operator for which the operands can be converted (something like "dense * sparse", but where only "dense * dense" and "sparse * sparse" are implemented, so it chooses one of those two, and converts one operand). At least that's my general understanding of the issue; the precise actual details may be quite different...

As Daniel says, it may be worth bringing this up on some R list...

Finn
>
